verdicts.note: Inventory of classical CV tasks (denoise, super-res, classification, segmentation, depth, pose, gaze). Ends with multimodal tasks (T2I, captioning, VQA) but only as 1-figure visual slides without content; book already covers these in Ch 22 and beyond.
Course project rubric (KITTI, ORB, YOLO, distortion robustness study). Not book material.
Human eye anatomy, Weber-Fechner, Mach bands. Pure biology and psychophysics, off-topic for LLM/agents.
Electromagnetic spectrum, CCD/CMOS sensor strips, illumination/reflectance. Pure sensing physics.
Tristimulus, CMYK, HSI, Bayer grid. Color science basics, not LLM-relevant.
Pinhole/thin-lens optics, projective geometry, vanishing points, depth-of-field. Pure camera geometry.
Image sampling/quantization, bilinear interpolation, false contouring. Standard DSP basics already implicit in audio/image chapters.
PIL, scikit-image, scipy.ndimage tutorial. Pure tooling intro.
Image slicing, blending, affine/projective transforms, salt-pepper noise. Library tutorial.
Bilinear/bicubic interpolation, antialiasing, median-cut color quantization. Pure image-processing tutorial.

verdicts.rationale: Harris corners, RANSAC, LoG/DoG/DoH blob detection. Classical hand-crafted features are the canonical 'what we used before learned features' contrast for Ch 22.1 (ViT patches as learned tokens replacing classical descriptors). One short callout in 22.1 would land well.
verdicts.weight: low (one paragraph or sidebar, no new section)

verdicts.rationale: HoG, SIFT (scale-space, position+orientation+128-dim descriptor), BRIEF, ORB, Haar features, Viola-Jones. SIFT scale-space and learned position+orientation encoding is a striking pre-deep-learning parallel to learned positional embeddings + patch tokens; BRIEF/ORB binary descriptors parallel modern binary embeddings. Useful sidebar for Ch 22.1.
verdicts.fit: Ch 22.1 (ViT tokenization) — 'classical descriptors vs learned patch embeddings' sidebar

verdicts.rationale: K-means vector quantization (VQ) for image color compression, PCA/eigenfaces, spectral clustering. K-means VQ is the direct precursor to VQ-VAE codebooks used in EnCodec/SoundStream (Ch 20 audio codecs) and to image tokenizers. Eigenfaces is a clean intuition for learned embeddings as linear-combination bases. Worth a callout in Ch 20.0.2 (audio codecs) and Ch 31.7 (embedding analysis).
verdicts.fit: Ch 20.0.2 audio codecs (VQ analogy), Ch 31.7 (PCA/embedding viz)

verdicts.note: k-NN, naive Bayes, SVM, AdaBoost, decision tree, random forest applied to MNIST and Viola-Jones faces. Classical ML basics, already implicit in Appendix material; no specific LLM/multimodal hook.

verdicts.rationale: Foundational compression theory: data vs information, coding/interpixel/psychovisual redundancy, autocorrelation, RLE, RMS/SNR fidelity. Directly frames the codec/tokenizer analogy: neural audio codecs (EnCodec) and image tokenizers (VQ-GAN, MAGVIT) all exploit the same three redundancies and use similar fidelity criteria. Useful for Ch 20.0.2 audio codec intro.
verdicts.fit: Ch 20.0.2 (neural audio codecs) — 'compression theory primer' callout

verdicts.rationale: Huffman coding, LZW, bit-plane coding, gray coding. Huffman is the entropy-coding back-end behind EnCodec range coding; LZW is the conceptual ancestor of BPE tokenization (variable-length codes built on-the-fly). One small callout in 19.x (BPE) or 20.0.2 would tie the threads together.
verdicts.fit: Ch 19 BPE/tokenization (LZW analogy), Ch 20.0.2 (audio entropy coding)

verdicts.note: CAC, FAX run-length, linear predictive coding for grayscale. Specialised to binary/fax imagery; LPC for audio is already covered elsewhere if at all needed.

Delta modulation, optimal predictors, Lloyd-Max quantizer. Lloyd-Max is the classical scalar quantizer, but the VQ-VAE/RVQ thread in audio chapters is already framed through neural VQ; this content is too narrow to add.

verdicts.rationale: DCT, Walsh-Hadamard, KLT, information packing, zonal vs threshold coding, wavelet coding. Transform coding is the conceptual parent of ViT patch tokenization (image broken into 8x8 / 16x16 blocks, transformed, quantized) and of audio sub-band codecs. KLT is the optimal energy-compaction transform and a clean way to motivate why learned tokenizers work. STRONG fit for Ch 22.1 ViT framing and Ch 20.0.2 codec framing.
verdicts.fit: Ch 22.1 (ViT patches as transform coding generalisation), Ch 20.0.2 (audio sub-band codecs)
verdicts.weight: medium (one shared sidebar plus figure across two chapters)

verdicts.rationale: JPEG (DCT + zigzag + Huffman), JPEG2000 wavelet, PNG/GIF LZW, MPEG I/P/B-frame video compression with motion vectors. I/P/B-frame motion compensation is the direct conceptual ancestor of video diffusion frame-conditioning and causal video tokenization (Ch 20.6-20.10 video). JPEG is the classic '8x8 patch transform + quantize + entropy code' that prefigures image tokenizers. STRONG analogy potential.
verdicts.fit: Ch 20.6-20.10 (video gen, I/P/B framing), Ch 22.1 (image tokenization analogy)
verdicts.weight: medium (one short sidebar; mention I/P/B in video chapter)

verdicts.note: Hough transform for lines and circles. Pure classical CV technique, no LLM/multimodal hook.

Otsu thresholding, watershed, Felzenszwalb, SLIC, Quickshift, active contours (snakes), GrabCut. Classical pixel-level segmentation; modern semantic segmentation and SAM are covered separately if at all.

verdicts.rationale: Brightness consistency, Lucas-Kanade, multiscale pyramid LK, Farneback dense flow. Optical flow is the classical 'what moved where between two frames' primitive that modern video diffusion implicitly learns. Useful as a brief callout in Ch 20.6-20.10 video generation when motivating temporal consistency, and as the historical baseline before flow-matching/RAFT-style learned flow.
verdicts.fit: Ch 20.6-20.10 (video gen — temporal coherence / motion modelling)

verdicts.note: Two-view stereo, epipolar geometry, fundamental/essential matrix, rectification, disparity. Pure classical geometric CV.

verdicts.rationale: Structure from Motion pipeline: SIFT/ORB matching, essential matrix, triangulation, bundle adjustment. COLMAP-style SfM is the standard pose backbone for NeRF/3DGS training (acknowledged in 3863 deck slide 13-14). If Ch 23 (Neural Scenes) discusses NeRF/3DGS data prep, a one-sentence mention of SfM/COLMAP as the upstream pose source belongs there.

verdicts.note: Point cloud capture and ICP alignment. Classical 3D registration; not directly tied to LLM-driven 3D scene generation.
Active stereo with projected patterns (Kinect). Pure sensing technique.

verdicts.rationale: Full 3D Gaussian Splatting walkthrough: scene representation as millions of Gaussians, 3D-to-2D projection, ray-space transformation, Taylor expansion, tile-based rasterization, adaptive density control, spherical-harmonics view-dependent color, training pipeline with gsplat / nerfstudio. Book has Ch 23 (3D Generation and Neural Scenes); this is exactly the material that chapter should cover. STRONG candidate for incorporation as Ch 23 section/subsection.
verdicts.fit: Ch 23 (3D Generation and Neural Scenes) — full subsection
verdicts.weight: high (entire 24-slide deck maps onto a new Ch 23 subsection on 3DGS)

verdicts.rationale: 2D Gaussian Splatting (flat oriented disks for better surface geometry). Direct extension of 3DGS deck above and a natural companion subsection in Ch 23.

Full NeRF: volume vs surface rendering, MLP architecture, position encoding (Fourier features defeating spectral bias — directly relevant to transformer positional encodings), hierarchical volume sampling, COLMAP integration, full volume-rendering math (transmittance, alpha compositing, ray marching). Book has Ch 23 (3D Generation and Neural Scenes); this is the foundational technique. The position-encoding slide alone (spectral bias, sin/cos basis) is a clean parallel to ViT/transformer positional encoding worth a cross-reference from Ch 22.
verdicts.fit: Ch 23 (NeRF foundation subsection), Ch 22.1 (positional encoding cross-reference)
verdicts.weight: high (entire 24-slide deck maps onto a new Ch 23 subsection on NeRF)

verdicts.rationale: Single-object trackers (Boosting, MIL, MOSSE, KCF, TLD, MEDIANFLOW, CSRT, GOTURN), motion vs appearance models, multi-object tracking. Tracking is the classical pre-cursor to temporal coherence in video diffusion and to multi-frame VLM understanding. Lighter fit than the 3D decks; a single sidebar in Ch 20.6-20.10 (video) noting 'classical trackers preserved identity across frames; modern video models learn this implicitly' would suffice.
verdicts.fit: Ch 20.6-20.10 (video gen / video understanding) — short callout

verdicts.rationale: Perspective-n-Point (PnP), P3P, Rodrigues/Euler rotation representations, PnP+RANSAC. Pose estimation is a foundational primitive for any agent that must reason about its own location (robotics, VLA). If Ch 24 (VLA / robotics) discusses spatial grounding or world models, a one-paragraph callout on PnP-style pose estimation as the classical localisation primitive would land.

Monocular SLAM: front-end feature matching + motion estimation, back-end bundle adjustment, loop closure with bag-of-words. SLAM is the canonical 'localize + map' primitive for embodied agents (Ch 24 VLA/robotics). Modern VLA work increasingly integrates SLAM-style spatial memory; a sidebar or short section in Ch 24 referencing classical visual SLAM as the geometric scaffold would tie it together.
verdicts.weight: low-medium (one short section or extended sidebar)
